key_facts: Devon's third quarter results were outstanding, showcasing the power of its Delaware focused asset portfolio and the benefits of its financially driven business model.
Devon's team's focus on operations excellence led to capturing efficiencies, accelerating free cash flow, reducing leverage, and returning a market-leading amount of cash to shareholders.
Devon's 2022 upstream capital program is planned to be in the range of $1.9 billion to $2.2 billion, with a WTI breakeven price of around $30.
Devon expects cash flow growth of more than 40% compared to 2021 at today's prices, with an 18% free cash flow yield at an $80 WTI price.
Devon has authorized a $1 billion share repurchase program through year-end 2022, equivalent to approximately 4% of its current market capitalization.
Devon's free cash flow in the third quarter was more than eightfold compared to previous periods, and the company reduced net debt by 16%.
Devon's implied dividend yield in 2022 is more than double that of the energy sector and more than seven times higher than the average company in the S&P 500 Index.
Devon's Delaware Basin assets account for roughly 80% of its capital deployment, with 13 operated rigs and four frac crews running during the quarter.
Devon's Boundary Raider project achieved initial 30-day production rates of 7,300 BOE per day, with over 60% being oil.
Devon's Cobra project in Lea County outperformed predrill expectations by more than 10%, with the top well achieving 30-day rates as high as 6,300 BOE per day.
Devon's high-margin oil production in the Delaware Basin grew 39% year over year, with average D&C costs improving to $554 per lateral foot in the third quarter.
Devon has a concentrated 300,000 net acre position in the liquids-rich window of the Anadarko Basin, with a joint venture agreement with Dow providing drilling carry.
Devon's financial strategy includes a fixed plus variable dividend framework, with the board approving a 71% increase in dividend payout to $0.84 per share.
Devon retired over $1.2 billion of outstanding notes this year and built a $2.3 billion cash balance at quarter end, reaching a debt-to-EBITDA leverage target of one turn or less.
Devon expects to retire approximately $1.0 billion of low-premium debt in 2022 and 2023 using cash already accumulated on the balance sheet.
Devon's financial strategy includes a share buyback program, which will be executed opportunistically when equity trades at a discounted valuation to historical multiples.

Devon's third quarter operating cash flow totaled $1.6 billion, an increase of 46% compared to last quarter, and generated $1.1 billion of free cash flow, the highest amount ever recorded in a single quarter.
Devon's financial strategy is working well, with excellent liquidity and substantial free cash flow generation, positioning the company to significantly grow its dividend payout over the next year.
Devon has a deep inventory of opportunities in the very best U.S. resource plays, with more than a decade of low-risk and high-return inventory in the Delaware Basin.

Devon is meeting the demands of investors, the market, and society by demonstrating capital discipline, earnings and cash flow growth, market-leading dividend payout, debt reduction, and a share buyback program.
